answer.rationale: The competitor's price cut creates immediate churn pressure on price-sensitive SMBs, but exp_73 shows promotional pricing acquires cohorts with -12% 30-day retention—a long-term value trap. The durable memory confirms that activation_messaging (memory_91) and simplified onboarding (memory_31, memory_86) drive engagement and time-to-value without eroding retention. These create genuine product stickiness in the SMB segment by accelerating first meaningful action. A standard_experiment deploying activation messaging to at-risk SMB accounts offers: (1) immediate response to churn without discounting, (2) evidence alignment with sustainable growth objective, (3) lower risk than promotional pricing. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well in established customers but do not address acute churn in price-sensitive new/at-risk cohorts. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is out-of-scope for this segment. The decision preserves uncertainty by testing rather than broad rollout, and avoids the documented retention cliff of discounting.
